data.name: Salvaged
data.detailed_description:
The human race explores the stars, but a keen focus on the future has left a trail of desolation in the past. You are Alex Pieterson, commander of the salvage ship Thaddeus and its team of hardened agents. You are a remnant of that past, fighting for survival in a huge new galaxy.

Salvaged is a strategy game designed to be played in both virtual reality and with regular 2D screens. The game’s first-person command view is a unique take on the genre, allowing the player to see the world of Salvaged literally through the eyes of Commander Pieterson.

  • Story-focused campaign - Salvaged features an original story-focused campaign mode penned by Daniel Hunter-Dowsing, a twisting narrative that integrates seamlessly with the game’s crew and combat systems.

  • Command your agents - Take command with unique real-time combat mechanics that force you to think on your feet. Plus, view the action through each of your agent’s head-cams in classic Hollywood style.

  • Upgrade and customise - Your team of Salvagers will become a personal squad of expert alien hunters. Make them your own with customisable skills, weapons and armour. Adapt your team to fit your strategy.

  • A deep new universe to explore - Salvaged takes place in a universe torn apart by warfare, pestilence and greed. The human race explores the stars, but a keen focus on the future has left a trail of desolation in the past.

  • Designed for both VR and regular play - Salvaged has been developed with virtual reality at the fore, designed to immerse you in your role as the commander of the salvage ship Thaddeus. However, the game can also be enjoyed without a VR headset, allowing anyone to experience the tactical gameplay and story-driven campaign.

reviews.review:
EDIT: It has now been over 5 years since my initial review. The "Early Access" game has recieved no updates. Save your money for something more active.


This review is bound to be out-of-date pretty fast, but this was mainly written on (12-13-2016).

Okay, I've played quite a bit now. This game has a bit of a "leg up" on other early access games, because it's playable, right out of the gate. There's a campaign (probably) an ending, and everything you *need* for a modern game.

But there's quite a bit of problems. First off, the game is VERY slow-paced. I hope you don't have stuff to do, because the tutorial alone is 30 minutes long. Not kidding. You also can't skip that tutorial, even after you've already gone through it on another save. After each mission, you HAVE to listen to a long conversation between yourself and your AI, who treats you like it's "Baby's first starship". That isn't too big a deal, but the game doesn't give you your "mission rewards" or let you choose or look through your next mission until you've sat through a usual 1-5 minute cutscene. This means that if you're low on money, then you can literally do nothing until the cutscene is over, and your money is given.

The cutscenes are actually quite high quality. I just wish they had subtitles, and that there was more I could to do move things along, or organize my crew during the cutscene.

The mouse movement feels odd. It's easily half the senstivity that I had in my desktop, outside of the game. I wish that mouse movement wasn't changed at all, since it feels much worse how it is. It would be nice if you could move around in the scene with your "game controls", since not being able to move eventually feels a bit claustrophobic, but I can see why you can't, since it would probably break the whole "VR", thing.

The "Strategy" part of this game, is also lacking. More often than not, I would position my squad as close to the door as possible, regardless of cover, since that generally would injure my soldiers less, and speed things up. This is due to the majority of "melee-only" troops in the first missions. Once I started encountering ranged-troops, It got a bit more difficult, but overall I was disappointed with the lack of strategic options. You can't tell your units to take cover, and switching between "ATK" and "DEF", usually results in taking more damage. I was pleased to find you could use "ATK" to have a soldier tank for your squad. Once my squad was wiped out due to a robot shooting them through a wall. They couldn't see the robot, and just took the damage until death. On occasion, I would see my troops, and enemies walk through walls. The pathfinding could use some work.

Sometimes I would order my units to stop breaching, and go to the teleporter. This would result in my troops trying to walk to the teleporter, and trying to walk back to the breach position. It takes probably twice as long. I wish I could switch out of "breach" without breaching and/or retreating out. Sometimes I would tell my soldier to retreat, just to have them get stuck on some geometry and die while the rest of the squad retreats.

TL;DR: The game is better than most straight out of early-access. But it's certainly not a "full game" yet. It needs a LOT of work. The presentation is fantastic, and high quality, but for that reason the rest of the game suffers. You should wait a while before buying, to find a much better game in the coming months.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 SP1 64 bit or newer
  • Processador: Intel Core i3-3225 @ 3.30GHz or equivalent
  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 660 2GB / AMD Radeon HD 7850 2GB
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 7 GB de espaço livre
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR or Oculus PC. Keyboard or gamepad required
  • Notas adicionais: These are recommended minimum requirements for non-VR. Salvaged is an Early Access game, and recommended requirements may change during development.
